Evidence is under `docs/audit/data/` and `docs/audit/probes/`; the severity,

without a file behind it.

## Severity classes

| class | meaning |
|---|---|
| S0 | **silent wrong answer** — compiles, links, runs, answers differently than php. Ranked above everything because it poisons every other measurement: a green build is actively misleading. |
| S1 | runtime hard failure — crash, uncaught throw, or a `return 0` link-stub that explodes later |
| S2 | compile or link hard failure, or a compiler crash |
| S3 | static finding with no observed runtime effect |
| S4 | advisory / analyzer residue |

**24 findings**: 2 S1, 11 S2, 9 S3, 2 S4.

Capability probes: 9 COMPILE, 1 CRASH, 9 DIFF, 7 PASS (`docs/audit/data/capability.tsv`).

| `toplevel-conditional-return-ends-program` | `include-semantics` | `tests/aot/cases/include_conditional_return/main.php` | a top-level `return` NESTED IN AN `if` inside any non-entry file terminated the WHOLE PROGRAM, so the entry never ran and the binary silently did nothing. lower_module flattens every file top-level statements into one __main with the entry last, and dropped a non-entry `return` only when it WAS a top-level statement; one nested in an `if` survived the flatten. The shape is composer own: vendor/autoload.php returns the loader and every symfony polyfill bootstrap is a version-guarded `return require`. It is why the first LINKING tier-1 run produced an empty stub list - with main empty the module was entirely dead-code-eliminated, so the tier read as complete having measured nothing. Fixed by rewriting every top-level return, at ANY depth, into "store the value, jump to a label at the end of this file": the statements stay in __main so top-level variables keep sharing one scope exactly as php include does, which is why it is a jump and not a synthetic per-file function. A valueless `return` stores NULL (php answer for one that RAN) while a file falling off its end still gives int(1), and the slot is seeded with int(1) UNCONDITIONALLY before the file body - which is also the only thing guaranteeing the slot global exists, since every write inside a version-guarded `if` now folds away with its branch. Two self-host traps on the way: reading a subclass field off a base Stmt SEGFAULTED the compiler while Zend compiled the same program fine, and returning an array OF arrays erased the inner element type and SIGBUS-ed the Zend-seeded compiler while the self-hosted build stayed green |
| `composer-autoload-roots-overlap` | `audit-tooling` | `src/Manticore/Main.php` | a file covered by two composer autoload roots was compiled TWICE and clang rejected the module with an invalid redefinition of the stub class constructor. symfony polyfills map psr-4 to the PACKAGE ROOT and then classmap a subdirectory of it, and the existing guard compared directory STRINGS, so a nested root was never equal to its parent. Deduped by FILE PATH instead, which is robust to any overlap. Not audit-only: any project whose autoload roots nest hits it |
| `composer-exclude-from-classmap-ignored` | `audit-tooling` | `src/Manticore/Main.php` | composer autoload.exclude-from-classmap was ignored, so shipped-but-excluded code was compiled. 51 of the 99 packages in the corpus declare it, almost always /Test/ or /Tests/, and those directories hold PHPUnit test-case base classes whose parent is a DEV dependency that --no-dev never installs: symfony/service-contracts ServiceLocatorTestCase extends TestCase and the tier-1 module failed on an undefined assertFalse. Now honoured, scoped to the package that declared it - one package saying /Test/ says nothing about another, and over-exclusion is a regression exactly as over-inclusion is |
| `guarded-define-not-registered` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/guarded_define.php` | a define guarded by if-not-defined never registered the constant, so a later bareword reference was a hard MIR.lower unknown-constant error. That is THE polyfill idiom - 45 guarded defines across the tier-1 packages, every one with this exact shape and not a version conditional among them - and it reached lowering through a DEFAULT PARAMETER VALUE, which must be a compile-time constant. It blocked 9 of 21 tier-1 packages, i.e. the entire polyfill layer. Only this shape is admitted and only for the SAME name the guard tests, which is what makes it sound without evaluating anything: the constant world is closed at compile time, so "nobody else defined N" is decidable. An unconditional define still wins and a duplicate never overwrites - which is also what makes the case that actually occurs harmless, a polyfill shipping both bootstrap.php and bootstrap80.php with whole-program AOT compiling both |
| `version-guard-not-folded` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/guarded_define.php` | foldGuard folded strict equality between compile-time constants but not ORDERED comparisons, so a PHP_VERSION_ID range guard stayed a runtime branch and its body was lowered. Those bodies DECLARE CLASSES, which lowering does not support as a statement, so tier 1 died on "unsupported statement kind Class" inside the polyfill-php85 NoDiscard stub. Folding is also the only correct answer - this compiler targets 8.5, so the shim must not exist and declaring it anyway would shadow the real thing. Deliberately not routed through a nullable-int helper: a nullable scalar null does not read back as null under the self-host, the same trap the tri-state guard encoding exists for, so the operands stay as the tagged string keys constScalarKey already produces |
| `local-preallocation-walk-not-exhaustive` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/assign_in_isset_index.php` | preallocateLocals was a hand-written list of node kinds, and a kind missing from it is not a missed optimisation but INVALID IR: the local StoreLocal emits a store with an EMPTY pointer operand and clang rejects the module with "expected instruction opcode", pointing at the following line. An assignment inside an isset() subscript in symfony/polyfill-intl-messageformatter was one such kind; a static call args had already been patched the same way earlier, one bug at a time. Every kind not special-cased now recurses over its children generically, so the walk is exhaustive by construction. Safe against the one case that would be wrong: Walk::children of a CLOSURE yields its captures, never its body, so a StoreLocal belonging to a nested frame cannot take a slot in this one |
| `audit-smoke-entry-named-nothing` | `audit-tooling` | `tools/audit/gen_manifest.php` | the tier smoke entry guessed each package root namespace from its DIRECTORY NAME, and every guess was wrong, so it printed "0 root classes live". That is not a cosmetic zero: class_exists on a name declared nowhere folds to false at compile time, so the entry referenced nothing and could not do the one job it has, which is to keep the tier reachable so dead-code elimination cannot empty the stub list. It now reads a REAL declared class out of each package, column-0 only so a stub inside a version guard is never picked (that guard folds false on a current target and the class does not exist), skipping the Test and stub directories composer excludes from its own classmap. T1 went from 0 to 9/20, and the count is now the evidence the tier is actually linked |
| `trait-static-prop-unregistered` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/trait_static_prop.php` | a trait STATIC property was never registered. Both the slot loop and the global-cell loop in LowerClasses walk the class OWN declarations, so `self::$traitStatic` had no registration and lowering refused the whole expression with "unsupported expression kind StaticAccess". It hard-blocked tier 2: symfony/cache AbstractAdapter keeps its $createCacheItem and $mergeByLifetime closures in statics inherited from AbstractAdapterTrait. php gives every USING CLASS its own slot - a trait is a compile-time copy, not shared storage - so registering under the using class name is exactly right and two classes using one trait get two counters. Registration and cell emission had to move together: registering the slot without emitting the cell left a load against a global nothing defined |
| `undefined-global-constant-is-compile-error` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/undefined_constant_throws.php` | FIXED. A reference to an undefined GLOBAL constant was a hard compile error where php defers it: php resolves a constant when the expression is EVALUATED and throws `Error: Undefined constant "X"` there, so a reference behind a guard that is false costs php nothing. symfony/cache reads \APC_ITER_KEY inside a method guarded by class_exists(\APCUIterator::class, false), and that one reference stopped an entire tier from building. It now lowers to a runtime throw carrying php own message, including the fully-qualified spelling php reports. Emitted as a codegen builtin rather than a prelude call ON PURPOSE: prelude demand is computed from the SOURCE TEXT, and a call the compiler synthesises appears in no source, so it could never gate itself in. Static detection is unaffected - the analyzer reports undefined.constant closed-world, which is where a typo belongs |
| `class-const-needs-absent-extension-constant` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/undefined_constant_throws.php` | FIXED by the same mechanism, and it turned out NOT to need lazy class constants after all. var-dumper AmqpCaster declares a const array keyed by \AMQP_DURABLE and friends; the worry was that a throwing reference inside a class-constant initializer would move the failure to STARTUP, since those initializers are evaluated eagerly. Measured instead of assumed: the class declares fine, startup is clean, and the Error is raised on the first READ of the constant - byte-exact with php, which reports the missing constant at exactly that point. The declared skip of the Caster directory was removed again |
| `conditional-class-decl-unregistered` | `language-core` | `tests/aot/cases/conditional_class_decl.php` | FIXED. A class declared inside a foldable `if` was registered NOWHERE. flattenConstantIfs hoists the live branch to the top level, but that runs AFTER both class-registration passes, and registerHoistedDecl handled FUNCTIONS only - so lowerClassMethods read classTable[name] for a key never added and handed the null to a ClassDef-typed parameter. Under Zend that is a warning plus a TypeError; self-built it is a SIGSEGV several frames from the cause, and it presented as a bare rc=139 out of a whole-program build. The shape is the ordinary way a package ships one class two ways: symfony/cache guards four exception classes on interface_exists(SimpleCacheInterface::class), declaring each in both arms. Hoisted decls now register like top-level ones, with their ClassDefs built after flattening completes so every decl is known before any def is built. lowerClassMethods also stops with the class NAME instead of dereferencing null - an ENUM stays exempt, because a method-less one legitimately has no ClassDef and every $cd read sits inside a loop that is empty for it |

## By owning epic

The ladder tier is the implementation order: a tier's dependency closure
lies entirely in lower tiers, so a gap first seen at tier N blocks tiers
N..8 and nothing below.

### `repr-consistency` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S1** `unhinted-static-prop-erased-slot` — an UNHINTED static property (`private static $x;`) has NO single static type, and read and store disagree about the same slot. emitStoreStaticProp NaN-boxes when the declared kind is CELL *or* UNKNOWN, but the READ stays typed `unknown` and the erased read path takes the raw word and guesses: a float comes back as int(4612811918334230528), and a STRING is inttoptr-ed from its tagged word and DEREFERENCED - `self::$x ??= 'v'; return self::$x;` is an outright SEGFAULT, which is the memoise idiom symfony/cache uses to hold its closures. `mixed` spells the same slot and is correct, because it types the slot CELL. Typing the unhinted form CELL to match was TRIED AND REVERTED: it is right for the scalars and WRONG for an ARRAY, which rides RAW through the very same slot, and static_array_prop_append went red at once. The encoding depends on the KIND STORED, so no single type on the read expresses it - this is the unknown/cell erasure root, and closing it wants the element-repr machinery, not a type swap. Severity raised from the original float-only report: it crashes, it does not merely misread

### `sapi-layer` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T3

- **S1** `superglobals-unseeded` — $_GET/$_POST/$_COOKIE/$_FILES/$_REQUEST are always []; $_SERVER carries a CLI shape with no web keys
- **S2** `globals-whole-array` — a whole-array $GLOBALS read is a hard compile error

### `parser-gaps` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S2** `parser-ref-in-array-literal` — PARTIAL: a reference inside an array literal now PARSES and carries byRef; lowering refuses it with a message that names the construct, replacing an "unexpected token: Ampersand" that pointed at a character and explained nothing. It is NOT honoured, and shipping the parse alone was rejected on the fn-by-ref precedent: an element that aliases is a property of the SLOT, and there is nowhere to record one. ARRAY_REPR_* (bits 1-3) and ARRAY_ELEM_HINT_* (bits 4-6) are WHOLE-ARRAY flags, and RefAddr_ binds a LOCAL to a slot address, never a slot to a source - the same missing fact behind vardump-ref-marker. polyfill-deepclone builds an alias pool it later writes back through, so a copy would silently lose every write. Closing it properly means a REF cell tag pointing at a {rc,value} box, the widen-to-cell machinery already on this branch to promote any ref-taken array element channel, and ~50 element-access emit sites learning to deref - its own worktree and a full gate. The parse-blocked skip in gen_manifest.php therefore STAYS, with its reason upgraded from a parse error to a named refusal
- **S2** `parser-byref-arrow-fn` — PARTIAL: `fn &()` / `function &()` now PARSE and carry returnsByRef; lowering refuses them with a precise message instead of compiling silently wrong code. Shipping the parse alone was measured and rejected — the alias came back a COPY, so $r = &$f(); $r[] = x left the original untouched. The missing half is the closure ABI, not the parser: named functions and methods already return by reference correctly

### `spl-classes` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S2** `spl-classes-absent` — PARTIAL: the 10 missing SPL EXCEPTIONS are declared with php parentage (BadMethodCall/Domain/Length/BadFunctionCall under LogicException; OutOfBounds/Overflow/Range/Underflow/UnexpectedValue under RuntimeException; JsonException under Exception). Still absent: the SPL ITERATORS and DirectoryIterator/DOMDocument/ReflectionExtension

### `language-core` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T2

- **S2** `undecidable-guard-class-decl` — a class or trait declared inside an `if` whose guard is NOT compile-time decidable is a hard compile error ("unsupported statement kind Class"). symfony/cache Redis62ProxyTrait declares the SAME trait in both arms of version_compare(phpversion('redis'), '6.2.0', '>='), and phpversion() of an absent extension is a runtime call this compiler does not fold. Distinct from the foldable case, which is now closed: there the live arm is known and hoisted. Here both arms declare one name and AOT can hold only one, so picking an arm silently is exactly the class of wrong answer the fn-by-ref precedent rejects. The principled fix is to decide the guard from the COMPILE-TIME world - the binary genuinely will not have ext-redis, so the else arm is the true one - which means folding phpversion()/version_compare() over the known extension set the way extension_loaded already folds. Currently the last blocker between tier 2 and a stub list

### `reflection-tier4` — 6 finding(s), first bites at T3

- **S2** `refl-param-attributes` — ReflectionParameter::getAttributes absent; DI autowiring and controller argument resolution cannot work
- **S2** `refl-param-default` — ReflectionParameter::getDefaultValue/getDeclaringClass absent
- **S2** `refl-union-type` — no ReflectionUnionType / ReflectionIntersectionType
- **S2** `refl-enum-absent` — ReflectionEnum absent; doctrine enum types and form choices need it
- **S2** `refl-hydration` — newInstanceWithoutConstructor absent; doctrine hydration and var-exporter need it
- **S3** `refl-attr-is-instanceof` — ReflectionAttribute::IS_INSTANCEOF is declared but the filter matches exact names only

### `pdo-sqlite` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T6

- **S2** `pdo-absent` — no PDO, PDOStatement, PDOException or sqlite binding exists at all

### `selfhost` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S3** `compiler-must-not-need-stubbed-symbols` — a compiler-side dependency on any symbol that link_stubs.sh stubs is invisible everywhere except the self-hosted build. sha1() was the instance (EVP_sha1 -> return 0), and the failure mode was a SEGFAULT in a compiled program, several removes from the cause. 43 symbols are stubbed in a self-host link — the crypto family, iconv, pcre2 and the fiber asm among them — and the compiler must not depend on ANY of them for a decision it bakes into output. A scan of src/ outside Runtime/Stdlib found no other use

### `platform-parity` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S3** `linux-only-difftest-diffs` — three cases diverge from php on LINUX but match byte-for-byte on macOS: runtime_env, ini_session_defaults, string_gaps. None of them touch anything this session added — they were simply never seen, because difftest had never been run on this branch on either platform. Pre-existing and platform-specific, which per the standing rule (a tier whose finding set differs across platforms is itself a finding) is exactly the class that must not be left implicit

### `error-handling` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T0

- **S3** `diagnostic-format-vs-php` — difftest flags error_handler_basic and trigger_deprecation_shape, and both are pure diagnostic FORMAT: php CLI emits every notice TWICE (once prefixed `PHP Notice:  `, once `Notice: `) and names the file by ABSOLUTE path, while manticore emits once with the path as written. The suite passes because its expected files encode our shape; only raw php parity sees it. Pre-existing, and adjacent to the no-warnings-throw-exceptions north star rather than a bug under it
- **S3** `function-exists-lies` — NEARLY CLOSED: was 44 of 53 common functions answering false; now 5. Fixed by teaching functionIsKnown the codegen builtins, the rest of the emitBuiltin dispatch and the compiler rewrites. The 5 left are DEMAND-GATED prelude names (error_reporting, register_shutdown_function, set_error_handler, ob_start, ob_get_clean) that the program only MENTIONS inside function_exists without calling — the prelude is then never injected. Measuring caught an over-inclusion too: `print` is a construct php does not expose, so claiming it exists was a regression of its own

### `autoload-semantics` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S3** `autoload-queue-never-drained` — PARTIAL: spl_autoload_register/unregister/functions now exist (prelude/autoload.php), so composer ClassLoader::register() compiles and registers instead of being a hard compile error. class_exists($n, true) still does not DRAIN the queue: the lookup is an emit-time fold into a static table and the guard machinery depends on it staying constant-foldable, so firing it is a design call. Bounded impact — ahead of time an autoloader can never define a class, so only the callback side effects are lost

### `references` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S3** `vardump-ref-marker` — var_dump does not mark a slot that IS a reference: php prints &int(99) for $a[1] after $r = &$a[1], manticore prints int(99). The ALIAS itself is correct — the value changes through the reference — so this is a display divergence, but it is the same missing fact (which slot is a reference) that a `[&$a[$k], $v]` literal would have to preserve, which is why parser-ref-in-array-literal is not just a parser gap

### `include-semantics` — 2 finding(s), first bites at T4

- **S3** `include-of-runtime-generated-file` — a file WRITTEN AT RUNTIME and then required can never work ahead of time — it is not one of the program's compile units, and no amount of path resolution changes that. Recorded rather than dropped because the original probe was written that way (file_put_contents then require) and a row that vanishes is indistinguishable from one never written. The probe was replaced with build-time-present fixtures keeping both real-world shapes: a file returning an array and a file returning a closure
- **S3** `include-once-repeat-not-tracked` — a REPEAT require_once/include_once returns php's bool(true); under the eager model every file's top-level code has already run inline, so nothing tracks that a unit was entered twice and the repeat re-reads the value slot instead. Bounded: the value is the same one, so only the true-vs-value distinction diverges. Closing it needs the lazy per-file unit model with a _once guard, which changes when every file's top-level code runs and wants its own worktree and a full gate

### `analyzer` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T1

- **S4** `analyzer-use-function` — the analyzer does not model `use function Ns\name` imports; 10 sites, code compiles and runs

### `regex-surface` — 1 finding(s), first bites at T2

- **S4** `preg-match-cell-boxing-cost` — preg_match $matches had to become cell-element so PREG_OFFSET_CAPTURE can hold its [text,offset] pairs; measured 0.088s -> 0.102s (+16%) on a 300k-iteration match loop. Recoverable by specializing on a constant $flags argument, which is compiler work, not stdlib work
